answer: AI agents managing cargo along a river jetty and lotus terminal resist Sybil attacks using memory-hard proof-of-work functions. To register, each node repeatedly traverses a large pseudorandom table in RAM, rendering zero-cost identity generation a fable. An attacker incurs the verifiable hardware cost of dedicated memory bus bandwidth per active identity. A key limitation is that high-bandwidth enterprise memory architectures still grant well-funded adversaries an efficiency advantage.
